alignments.note: Infinitive absolute takes the distinct adverbial word written for it (rule 56).
Waw plus prohibitive rendered by the single word 'neither', which carries both the coordination and the negation; headed on the negative (rules 23, 35).

The excess adverb is written inside the single English word 'overwise', which cannot be divided between the verb and yôṯēr; the two share one unit headed on the verb and on that word (rule 30). Competing reading: give 'overwise' to the verb alone and mark yôṯēr unrepresented, which rule 30 forbids for a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a fused word.
לָמָּה rendered by the single word 'why'; headed on the interrogative that carries the lexeme (rule 30).
Finite verb with modal and subject pronoun; the reflexive renders the verb's own stem sense and stays with it (rules 17, 44).

review_notes: The verse writes the excess twice, once as a separate word ('overmuch' for harbēh) and once inside 'overwise'; the second is treated as a rule 30 fusion, with the alternative named in that unit's note.
